editorial_note: For the sixth morning running, GitHub listed the same sixteen projects in the same order, and every one has been featured here before, so there are no first-time cards. Four return because ==something material changed since their cards==: OpenVINO merged a vLLM backend and support for the Inkling 2 models, Firecrawl switched off by default the admin routes that carry their key in the URL, MiniMind fixed a reward penalty that ignored repeated Chinese text, and Cursor's plugin catalogue grew to 160 entries. Curation order reflects practical interest, not GitHub rank. Trending is not a release date or an endorsement.
coverage_notes: GitHub's daily listing held 16 rows at capture, the same sixteen repositories in the same order as on 23 to 27 November. The capture parsed exactly sixteen listing rows and is GitHub's own list, not a truncation by us.

All 16 listing entries were inspected. Exact public GitHub API metadata, releases since the previous morning's check and default-branch commits since 07:00 UTC on 27 November were read between 07:01:36 and 07:02:02 UTC; pull requests and release notes for the likely picks between 07:02:16 and 07:02:47 UTC, and their README files at 07:02:35-07:02:37 UTC. For the two picks last featured on 18 November, commits and releases since that card were also read. Every checked repository was active and unarchived.

Returning picks: openvinotoolkit/openvino (cards of 21 and 24 November) merged the vLLM torch.compile integration (pull request 36346) at 00:58 UTC on 28 November and Inkling 2 GGUF support (pull request 40393) at 23:17 UTC on 27 November; firecrawl/firecrawl (cards of 20 and 24 November) merged header-only admin access (pull request 5522) at 18:06 UTC on 24 November and the new default (pull request 5523) at 19:10 UTC on 27 November; jingyaogong/minimind (card of 18 November) merged the CJK repetition-penalty fix (pull request 950) on 21 November and optional warmup (pull requests 866 and 960) on 22 and 26 November; cursor/plugins (card of 18 November) went from 149 to 160 marketplace entries and added /reframe to pstack (pull request 1324) on 23 November.

Left out although they changed: Tracer-Cloud/opensre (cards of 23 and 25 November) published v0.1.2026.11.28 with an empty changelog; nginx/nginx (QUIC path and connection-id fixes and a mail shutdown fix, not released); mjmirza/app-store-compliance (card of 27 November; keyword and manifest-check fixes and a Play crypto-licensing note); google-labs-code/stitch-skills (two script fixes); toeverything/AFFiNE (a canary build and a Persian calendar fix); zhouxiaoka/autoclip (a code-signing policy document); elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter (a star-history chart refresh only).

Left out as unchanged: obra/superpowers (card of 18 November) has no commit or release on its default branch since that card; HKUDS/CLI-Anything (card of 15 October), cathrynlavery/diagram-design, mvanhorn/last30days-skill and XiaoYouChR/Ghost-Downloader-3 had no default-branch commit or release since the previous morning's check.
The preceding seven calendar dates, 21-27 November, were checked for local history; all seven editions exist.

The official listing was captured at 08:01:15 Europe/Paris. Literal stars-today labels are GitHub's displayed period figures; API total stars and README evidence were checked separately at the times shown per card. They are not an independently audited rolling 24-hour growth measurement.

Feature descriptions, test, benchmark and performance figures come from each project's own README, release notes and pull requests and are the maintainers' or contributors' claims. No candidate code, installer, CLI, package, plugin or model was installed, downloaded or run, and none of this is a security audit or endorsement.

projects.description: Intel's open-source inference toolkit: it ==converts and optimizes trained models== and runs them on CPUs, Intel GPUs and Intel NPUs.
projects.why_interesting: Material change since the 24 November card on GGUF conversion: overnight it merged ==a vLLM backend built on torch.compile==, which vLLM loads as a plugin and which runs on CPU once a deployment selects the openvino compile backend. A separate merge lets its GGUF frontend load ==Inkling 2 and Inkling 2 Mini== GGUF files, vision projector included, with outputs checked against llama.cpp in the pull request's tests.
projects.caveat: Both changes are ==on the master branch, not in a release==: the latest release is still 2026.4.1 of 1 October. The Inkling pull request itself says PagedAttention does not work yet and GPU decoding is very slow until a follow-up lands; the vLLM path is CPU only, and both pull requests say AI coding agents helped write them. No speed figure here was measured by us.

projects.description: A web scraping and crawling service for AI agents: it ==turns websites into clean Markdown== as a hosted API, a self-hosted server or the single-binary Firecrawl Local.
projects.why_interesting: Material change since the 24 November card, for anyone who self-hosts it: the admin routes and queue dashboard that ==took the admin key as part of the URL are now off by default==. A key in a URL tends to end up in access logs and proxies, and a change merged on 24 November already redacted it from Firecrawl's own logs and made every admin route answer with the key in a header under /admin/ops/, checked in constant time.
projects.caveat: Self-hosted setups whose monitoring still calls the old /admin/key/ addresses ==will stop getting answers== unless they set BULL_AUTH_KEY_PATH_ROUTES=true or switch to the header routes. This is on the main branch, not in a tagged release, and when the hosted service picks it up was not checked. The project is mainly AGPL-3.0, with MIT SDKs.

projects.description: A from-scratch course in training a small language model: it writes pretraining, fine-tuning and reinforcement learning out ==in plain PyTorch== for a 64M-parameter model.
projects.why_interesting: Back after our 18 November card because a contributor found that ==its repetition penalty missed repeated Chinese text==: the word splitter behind the penalty in the PPO, GRPO and agent RL scripts counted an unpunctuated run of Chinese characters as one word, so repeated phrases went unpunished. The fix splits Chinese, Japanese and Korean text per character and, by the pull request's own test, leaves English scores unchanged. Training can now also use an optional learning-rate warmup.
projects.caveat: Reinforcement-learning runs made with the earlier code ==largely escaped the repetition penalty on Chinese output==, and the before-and-after scores are the contributor's tests. A 64M model is a teaching tool, not a capable assistant; the main README is in Chinese, with an English translation.

projects.description: Cursor's plugin specification and catalogue: each plugin is ==a folder of skills, rules and MCP definitions== that the editor's agent can load.
projects.why_interesting: Back after our 18 November card, when the marketplace manifest listed 149 plugins: it ==listed 160 at our check==, with connectors such as FreshBooks, Easyship and Jobber added since. The pstack workflow plugin also gained /reframe, a skill that gives the expert terms and neighbouring fields for what you describe, each with a link it says it opens and cuts if unconfirmed.
projects.caveat: GitHub detects ==no license for the repository==: the README ends with an MIT line, but there is no root license file, so check each plugin. Connector plugins give an agent access to business data under your account, so review their scopes; one was added and reverted within ten minutes on 25 November. There are no releases or version tags.
